issues.legal_issue: A court must consider a plea that a transfer is prohibited by an absolute statutory bar even if the plea is raised at a later appellate stage.
material_facts: The land in dispute was raiyati land governed by the applicable regulation.
The plaintiffs challenged an exchange as prohibited by the regulation; the District Court judgment showed that the statutory contention had in fact been canvassed there.
The High Court declined to consider the contention, reasoning that it had been raised too late and that the opposing party might have raised factual answers earlier.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not entitled to refuse to consider the plea on those grounds; the statutory language required it to take notice of the contention if the prohibition applied.
issues.legal_principle: The regulation prohibited transfers of raiyati holdings and directed courts not to recognise transfers made in contravention of that prohibition. Because that direction was absolute, the court had to consider the plea even assuming it was first raised before it, provided the facts bringing the transaction within the prohibition were shown.

predicates.appellate_proceeding: The matter is before a court exercising appellate jurisdiction.
predicates.transfer_challenged_under_absolute_bar: A party challenges a transfer on the ground that an applicable absolute legal prohibition bars it.
predicates.plea_raised_at_appellate_stage: The party raises that challenge at an appellate stage.

issues.definition: When a party challenges a transfer under an absolute prohibition in an appeal, the appellate court must consider the challenge even if it is raised at that stage.

issues.legal_issue: The party relying on an exception to a prohibition on transfers must prove the facts establishing that exception after the challenger shows that the prohibition applies.
material_facts: The appellants showed that the exchanged lands were raiyati lands in the area governed by the regulation.
The regulation prohibited transfers unless the right to transfer was recorded in the record of rights.
The respondent relied on the possible existence of an entry recording the transferor's right to transfer, but the respondent bore the burden of establishing that exception.
issues.conclusion: Once the appellants showed that the lands were raiyati lands governed by the regulation, the respondent had to prove that the record of rights contained an entry permitting the transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 27(1) of the Sonthal Parganas Settlement Regulation, 1872, the challenger initially had to show that the prohibition applied. If the opposing party relied on the exception for a recorded right to transfer, that party bore the burden of proving the relevant entry.

predicates.civil_claim_challenging_land_transfer: A civil proceeding challenges the validity of a transfer of land.
predicates.challenger_shows_protected_land: The challenger shows that the land is of a kind subject to the transfer prohibition.
predicates.opposing_party_relies_on_transfer_except: The opposing party relies on an exception based on a recorded right to transfer the land.

issues.definition: In a civil challenge to a land transfer, once the challenger shows that the land is protected by a transfer prohibition, an opposing party relying on an exception must prove the facts establishing that exception.

issues.legal_issue: An exchange of land is a transfer subject to a prohibition that covers transfers by contract or agreement.
material_facts: A life estate holder exchanged raiyati lands for other lands while the statutory prohibition was in force.
The regulation prohibited transfers of a raiyat's interest by sale, gift, mortgage, lease, or any other contract or agreement.
The respondent argued that an exchange was not expressly named in the prohibition.
issues.conclusion: An exchange is a transfer within the scope of the prohibition, and the exchange in this case was invalid because the prohibition applied and no exception was established.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27(1) of the Sonthal Parganas Settlement Regulation, 1872, broadly covered transfers made by any contract or agreement. Under section 118 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, an exchange involves mutual transfers of ownership, and completion of an exchange requires a transfer in the manner provided for a sale. The court also referred to Jyotish Thakur v. Tarakan Jha in discussing the purpose and history of the prohibition.

rule.if: land_transfer_proceeding and protected_land and transaction_is_exchange and transfer_exception_not_proved

predicates.land_transfer_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the validity of a transfer of land.
predicates.protected_land: The transferred land is subject to a legal prohibition on transfers.
predicates.transaction_is_exchange: The parties mutually exchanged ownership of one property for another.
predicates.transfer_exception_not_proved: No applicable exception permitting the transfer has been established.

issues.definition: An exchange of protected land is invalid when the exchange is challenged and no applicable exception to the transfer prohibition is proved.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee cannot defeat a reversioner's right to recover property by relying solely on adverse possession attributable to a widow's acts or omissions during her limited estate.
material_facts: The property had been inherited by a widow from her husband as a limited owner.
The respondent claimed that possession following the exchange had continued long enough to establish adverse possession against the reversioners.
The plaintiffs were the next reversioners and brought their claim within twelve years after the widow's death.
issues.conclusion: The respondent could not rely on adverse possession during the widow's lifetime to defeat the reversioners' claim, and the claim brought within twelve years of the widow's death was not barred.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied Article 141 of the Limitation Act, 1908, and principles of Hindu law: a reversioner's right is in the nature of a spes successionis and is not traced through the widow, so the reversioner does not lose that right through the widow's negligence or sufferance. It relied on Kalipada Chakraborti v. Palani Bala Devi and referred to Mulla's Hindu Law.

predicates.reversioner_recovery_proceeding: The proceeding is brought by a reversioner to recover immovable property after the limited estate holder's death.
predicates.property_inherited_by_limited_estate_hol: The property was inherited by a person holding only a limited estate.
predicates.adverse_possession_depends_on_limited_ho: The opposing claim of adverse possession rests on possession arising from the limited estate holder's acts or omissions.
predicates.claim_brought_within_limitation_after_de: The reversioner's recovery claim is brought within the applicable limitation period measured from the limited estate holder's death.

issues.definition: A reversioner may recover property within the applicable period after the limited estate holder's death when the opposing claim of adverse possession rests on that holder's acts or omissions.

issues.legal_issue: The later repeal of a prohibition does not validate a transaction that was void when made under that prohibition.
material_facts: The exchange occurred while the regulation's transfer prohibition was in force.
The exchange was invalid under that prohibition.
issues.conclusion: The later repeal did not make the previously invalid exchange valid or binding.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that repeal of sections 27 and 28 by the Santal Tenancy (Supplementary Provisions) Act, 1949, could not render a transaction that was invalid and void when made into a valid and binding transaction.

predicates.transfer_prohibition_in_force_when_trans: A legal prohibition on the transfer was in force when the transaction occurred.
predicates.transaction_void_under_prohibition: The transaction was void under the prohibition when it occurred.
predicates.prohibition_later_repealed: The prohibition was repealed after the transaction occurred.

issues.definition: If a transaction was void under a prohibition in force when it was made, the later repeal of that prohibition does not validate the transaction.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory bar on civil suits concerning matters decided by a settlement officer does not apply when the validity of the transfer was neither raised nor decided in the settlement process.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a civil suit challenging the validity of the exchange under the transfer prohibition.
The validity of that exchange under the prohibition had not been raised before or determined by a settlement officer or court in the settlement process.
The respondent argued that section 11 of the regulation barred the suit.
issues.conclusion: Section 11 did not bar the civil suit because the validity of the exchange under the transfer prohibition had not been decided in the settlement process.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Sonthal Parganas Settlement Regulation, 1872, gives specified settlement decisions the force of civil court decrees and restricts later suits concerning matters so decided, subject to section 25A. It did not apply to a matter that had neither been agitated nor determined by a settlement officer or court.

predicates.civil_suit_challenging_transfer: A party brings a civil suit challenging the validity of a land transfer.
predicates.settlement_process_did_not_decide_transf: The validity of the challenged transfer was neither raised nor determined in the settlement process.

issues.definition: A civil suit challenging a transfer is not barred by a settlement-decision rule when the settlement process did not decide the transfer's validity.
